The plain reading of unreliable is recurring failures across reasonable tasks or variations, despite substantial competence. It does not mean inability to reason or performance below humans on every benchmark.
Psychological reasoning is operationalized through theory-of-mind tasks, which Marcus explicitly names.
Support requires evidence covering all three named domains.
criteria.support_condition: Original evaluations document recurring or substantial robustness failures by GPT-4 in physical, theory-of-mind and mathematical reasoning.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, varied evaluations establish consistently dependable GPT-4 reasoning in all three domains, with apparent failures explained by defective tests rather than model behavior.

evidence.explanation: NEWTON found uneven physical-attribute performance and identified a scenario where GPT-4 struggled to answer consistently. Its 87.7% average across scenario tasks is substantial counterweight: the result supports incomplete reliability, not general physical-reasoning incapacity.

GPT-4-0314 scored 97.5% on the original false-belief category but 0% on two altered unexpected-transfer categories. These sharp differences support unreliable transfer across psychological scenarios, while the original-task success limits any claim of general incapacity.

GSM-Plus tested GPT-4 among models solving original grade-school problems and controlled variations; successful original answers did not consistently transfer to altered problems. Multiple prompting methods improved performance but did not produce consistent robustness across the tested variations.

This study found GPT-4 matched or exceeded humans on several theory-of-mind tests, with weakness concentrated in faux-pas detection. Follow-up experiments attributed that weakness to excessive caution, cautioning against interpreting every wrong answer as an inability to infer mental states.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The mathematical robustness evaluation, available in this version on 2024-07-02, completes the cited evidence of recurring failures across all three domains.
